historical_commentary.text: This note introduces User Defined Forms, a 4D 2004 feature letting end users create or modify customized forms at runtime — even inside compiled, merged standalone applications — so vertical-market developers could let different clients tailor the look and feel of shared data views. The general goal (end-user-customizable UI without redeployment) remains a legitimate and still-pursued feature pattern in modern 4D applications, but the specific runtime form-customization mechanism described predates Project Mode, ORDA, and modern List Box/form object models, so a developer solving this problem today would very likely use different, more current tools.
related_updates: Later 4D versions introduced much richer object/List Box models and dynamic form-building capabilities that supersede the specific 2004 mechanism described here
Project Mode (4D v17, 2018) changed how forms are stored and could be programmatically manipulated compared to binary Design Mode structures
Modern 4D applications more often achieve end-user UI customization via dynamically configured List Box columns or JSON-driven UI definitions rather than the 2004-era User Defined Forms mechanism
